prize_parts.citation: For foundational contributions to the analysis of nominal rigidities and monetary policy: staggered price setting, interest-rate policy rules, and the micro-founded theory of optimal monetary policy.

statement.case_for: I keep B014 first after reading the openings. The New Keynesian framework joins three separable ideas: time-dependent price setting (Calvo), staggered contracts and a policy rule (Taylor), and a unified micro-founded normative theory of interest-rate policy (Woodford). Each has been used, taught and stress-tested for decades, and the framework is used operationally in central banks. It has also been confronted with data repeatedly. That includes the 2008 crisis, the zero lower bound and the post-2021 inflation, and the confrontation produced revisions and extensions rather than abandonment. I value that kind of durability because it is what survives scrutiny, not just early enthusiasm. Four of eleven members ranked it first and ten ranked it in their top three. I do not treat that as scientific merit. The more useful signal is that colleagues with very different specialities independently describe the same three conceptual roles (pricing friction, rule, synthesis) as the most distinct foundations. The proposed trio covers these roles with a concise citation that does not claim to credit the whole field.
statement.case_against: Attribution is the real weakness. Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Gertler and Smets all made major contributions, especially on estimation and empirical validation. A three-person cap therefore leaves out people whose work is arguably what made the framework credible against data. I also worry that the framework's empirical record is mixed. Identification in medium-scale DSGE models rests on strong structural assumptions, and the post-2021 inflation and the heterogeneous-agent critique are unresolved. The committee could reasonably judge that earlier macro and monetary prizes (Lucas, Sargent and Sims, Kydland and Prescott, Bernanke) have already covered much of this ground. I cannot independently verify the priority claims from the supplied evidence.

responses.point: Timo ranks B047 (Melitz and Helpman) first and prefers Woodford, Gali and Taylor in B014. He covers theory, the empirical and analytical framework, and the policy rule, and he notes that the field may be relatively saturated by earlier macro prizes.
responses.response: I agree with his reading of the three roles and that saturation is a fair worry. Where I differ is on Gali versus Calvo. Calvo's pricing mechanism is the element every New Keynesian model inherits, and it is more clearly a discrete originating contribution than Gali's theoretical and empirical development. Gali's case is strong and I treat the choice as genuinely close, but a prize citation naming the pricing friction, the rule and the synthesis is more defensible on priority. On B047, I rank it sixth, below B014. Melitz is a clean originator, but I see the Krugman 2008 overlap and the Bernard–Eaton–Kortum priority questions as costs that B014's attribution problem does not outweigh.

responses.point: Per ranks B003 first (Kiyotaki, Moore, with Gertler). He argues that collateral constraints are a foundational macro-finance mechanism that shaped understanding of the 2008 crisis and policy responses.
responses.response: I accept that B003 has the sharper attribution (the 1997 Kiyotaki–Moore paper is a clear origin) and that it is scientifically important. That is why I keep it as an alternative and ranked it fifth. My reservations are that direct empirical identification of the collateral channel is harder than the theory, and that the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises covers adjacent territory. I would not add Gertler to the pair, because that blurs the Bernanke–Gertler–Gilchrist lineage and overlaps with B014, where Gertler also appears. If the committee prefers a pair with a cleaner attribution, I would support B003 over a contested trio, but I think B014 has the greater breadth of use.

responses.point: Tommy ranks B006 first (Rubinstein and Wolinsky). He argues that alternating-offers bargaining is a foundational result with more than four decades of confirmation and no timing risk, and that Binmore is a plausible but less defensible third name.
responses.response: I agree that B006 is mature and conceptually elegant, and the Rubinstein–Wolinsky attribution is cleaner than most. Where I qualify is on how the evidence for the contribution is weighed. My own work stresses whether results hold up when tested, and B014's framework has been tested directly in policy use and in data, with the fallout visible. A theoretical bargaining result is durable, but its confirmation is largely through its role as a building block. Hassler's point that game theory has recently been rewarded (several prizes between 2005 and 2020) also matters to me. This is not a view that theory should lose to applied work. It is that, for this cycle, I find breadth of tested use more compelling, and I did not rank B006 among my top eight.

responses.point: Peter ranks B014 first with Woodford, Gali and Taylor, and ranks B018 (Piketty, Saez, Zucman) second. He values the durable data infrastructure and treats the debated wealth methods and policy advocacy as risks.
responses.response: We agree on B014 and differ only on whether Gali or Calvo takes the third place, which I regard as the key open question. On B018, I also rank it high (third), and I share his view that the top-income series is a durable public good. I would restrict credit to Piketty and Saez, since the wealth and offshore estimates are newer and the methods for allocating wealth are still contested. Adding Zucman now would credit a still-disputed strand. I would not weigh policy advocacy against the work, only the robustness of the measurements.

uncertainties: Whether the third B014 name should be Calvo (originating pricing friction) or Gali (theoretical and empirical development), with Christiano and Eichenbaum and Smets also excluded by the cap.
How much weight the committee gives the post-2021 inflation episode and the heterogeneous-agent critique when judging the framework's durability.
Whether earlier monetary and macro prizes (including 2022) leave enough room for B014 compared with a pair-based candidate such as B003.
Attribution and priority claims rest on background knowledge, not independent verification from the supplied evidence.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. None of the B014 credited names (Smets, Calvo, Taylor, Gali, Christiano, Gertler, Eichenbaum, Woodford) appears among my listed co-authors or networks. The same applies to the alternatives B003 and B032.
